title: Bears Overwhelm Panthers 59-37 in Week 1 Rushing Clinic
dek: The Chicago Bears defeated the Carolina Panthers 59-37 in Week 1, running the ball 39 times for 291 yards and six touchdowns while Caleb Williams added 269 passing yards and two scores. The Panthers' offense produced 361 passing yards and four total touchdowns but could not slow Chicago's ground attack.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Bears accumulated 39 rushing carries for 291 yards and six rushing touchdowns in a 59-37 Week 1 victory over Carolina.
bottom_line: The Panthers held their own through production but had no answer for Chicago's ground game. Week 2 will test whether the Bears can replicate this dominant rushing output against a different defensive scheme.
body:
The Chicago Bears defeated the Carolina Panthers 59-37 in Week 1, building a dominant offensive performance on the ground behind Ben Johnson's scheme. The Bears accumulated 39 rushing carries for 291 yards and six rushing touchdowns, per Yahoo Sports. Caleb Williams contributed 269 passing yards and two additional touchdowns through the air.
The Panthers' offense kept pace for stretches: Bryce Young passed for 361 yards and three touchdowns while adding a rushing touchdown, per Yahoo Sports. Yet Carolina's defensive output proved insufficient to contain Chicago's running game. The Panthers' inability to slow the Bears' ground attack stood out despite their own offensive production.
The Bears attempted a fourth-and-1 play from their own 21-yard line that yielded no gain, per Yahoo Sports.
Chicago won the NFC North last season when few expected a competitive run, per Yahoo Sports, establishing itself as one of the NFL's surprises. The Week 1 offensive showing offers an early indication that the Bears' offense remains formidable entering this campaign.
